note: Trainable: eligible for the fine-tune query distribution. Hartmann's compilation — Boehme quotations interleaved with theosophical commentary; probes drafted from the quoted Boehme material.

queries.query: Boehme's teaching that divine wisdom cannot be pulled down by wanting it, any more than we can drag sunlight to us — we can only step out of the shadow and ascend past where the clouds end
queries.note: The sunlight simile for receiving wisdom; 'neither can we attract the sunlight', 'climb to the top of the mountain which rises above the clouds' paraphrased away.

queries.query: Boehme on the seven qualities of eternal nature, each eternally generating the others, appearing in the power of the Word like seven burning lights
queries.note: The seven properties/spirits chapter; 'seven luminous torches', 'crystalline ocean', 'the last generates the first' paraphrased away; 'seven qualities of eternal nature' kept — the doctrine's own name.

queries.query: Boehme's account of his breakthrough: his sorrowing spirit rose up as if in a tempest and would not stop wrestling with God's love and mercy until the blessing came and the light broke through
queries.note: The autobiographical illumination passage; 'as if moving in a great storm, arose in God', 'carrying with it my whole heart and mind' paraphrased into indirect speech.

queries.query: why Lucifer fell according to Boehme: God's light did not push him out — his own imagination drew him into the fiery wrath he had kindled within himself, and he stayed in the qualities of that fire
queries.note: The Lucifer chapters; 'the wrath of nature' drawing him, 'imagine (project his consciousness) into the fire', 'remained in the qualities of the central fire which he had awakened' paraphrased away; 'Lucifer' kept as a name any reader knows.

queries.query: what happens to the soul after it separates from the body at death
queries.note: Boehme's death-and-eternal-life chapter answers this, but so does half the corpus. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: must a seeker abandon home, family, and possessions, or only the will that clings to them
queries.note: Renunciation as inner surrender rather than outward flight; answered by hindu, buddhist, stoic material too. No target — graded post-hoc.
